role.altitude: The cardiologist keeps examining, scanning, talking with patients and deciding treatments and tests; opening separate result screens, typing notes and measurements, copying referral data and tracking pending tests by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Validating scribe drafts quickly and carefully
role.ambitious_version: A cardiologist whose time with patients is no longer cut short by typing.

tasks.short: Review new results and device data, see and examine the patient, reevaluate treatments, document the visit, confer with the nurse and answer portal messages to monitor patients' conditions and progress.

steps.what: Cardiologist opens separate screens for results, vitals and device data since the last visit
Cardiologist sees and examines the patient to monitor the condition and progress
Cardiologist reevaluates treatments as necessary
Cardiologist types the follow-up visit note

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's agreement.
loop.output: A draft visit note in the department's structure.
loop.check: The cardiologist reads and corrects every line before it is saved in the record; a monthly sample is audited for omissions.
loop.stop: The cardiologist types the note when the recording is poor or the patient declines.
loop.why_not_simpler: The consultation is free speech; no form captures it.

steps.what: Cardiologist confers with the heart failure nurse on follow-up
Cardiologist answers patient portal messages about symptoms

tasks.design: A monitoring view in the patient record shows lab results, blood pressure, weight and readings from implanted or home devices as trends since the last visit, instead of the cardiologist opening each result screen and device portal. With the patient's agreement, a scribe drafts the visit note from the consultation; the cardiologist corrects every line before it is saved. Examining, reevaluating treatment and conferring stay with the cardiologist. No software proposes a treatment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results sat in separate screens and notes were typed after the visit.
tasks.enabler_now: Trend views in the record and scribes that write back to it.
tasks.still_hard: Device data from vendors without an interface.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a patient is more tired than the numbers say.

reach.learn: Whether the cardiologist looks at them more than the screen.

evidence.claim: A scribe records the consultation, the clinician validates, and the note goes into the patient record.
Across 236,153 scribe notes, self-estimated time per note fell 29%; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: monitoring and reevaluating; recording history at intake (task 22706) is in this set, and prescribing (task 22711) and talking to other physicians (task 22714) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: about 70% of results and device readings reach the record electronically; s1 is priced at that share.
A DPIA is done and the works council consents before the scribe is used.
Examining, reevaluating and conferring keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of patients who agree to recording.
research_questions: Do omissions in notes change after the scribe?

incremental.description: Cardiologist joins the monthly sample audit of notes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few patients agree to recording; high: most agree and devices are linked.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the patient and equipment, observe the ultrasound display screen and listen to signals, take measurements, record vascular information and flag urgent findings.

steps.what: Cardiologist prepares the patient and the ultrasound equipment
Cardiologist observes the ultrasound display screen and listens to Doppler signals
Cardiologist takes measurements on the ultrasound machine
Cardiologist types the vascular information from the machine screen into the report
Cardiologist flags urgent findings to the treating physician

tasks.design: The ultrasound machine sends its measurements as a structured report to the reporting system, where they fill the report fields, instead of the cardiologist typing values read off the screen. Scanning, listening, measuring and flagging findings stay with the cardiologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measurements were typed from the machine screen.
tasks.enabler_now: Ultrasound machines that export structured measurement reports.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a flow pattern that means a narrowing.

evidence.claim: Vitals, results and measurements arrive by integration rather than retyping.

assumptions: Boundary: observing and recording vascular information; comparing measurements to standards (task 22693) and calculating valve areas (task 22692) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s4: about 70% of ultrasound machines export structured measurements; s4 is priced at that share.
s4 saves the second entry of values shown on the machine.
Scanning and measuring keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of machines with structured export.
research_questions: Do transcription errors in reports fall?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: old machines; high: all machines export.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Have the patient complete a questionnaire, check patient identification, obtain history from referral records, take the history, examine the patient, record history and examination results, and check the note.

steps.what: Patient fills in a pre-visit questionnaire on history, medication and symptoms
Cardiologist checks patient identification and referral data
Cardiologist copies medical history and medication from referral letters and other hospitals' records
Cardiologist obtains the history from the patient in conversation
Cardiologist examines the patient
Cardiologist types the history and examination results in the record

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's agreement, and the questionnaire answers.
loop.output: A draft history and examination note in the department's structure.
loop.check: The cardiologist reads and corrects every line before it is saved; a monthly sample is audited for omissions.
loop.stop: The cardiologist types the note when the recording is poor or the patient declines.
loop.why_not_simpler: The history is free speech; no form captures it.

steps.what: Cardiologist checks and signs the note

tasks.design: Patients answer a pre-visit questionnaire in the patient portal. Medication and diagnoses from referrers and other hospitals arrive through structured exchange into the record, instead of being copied from letters. With the patient's agreement, a scribe drafts the history and examination note from the consultation and the questionnaire; the cardiologist corrects every line and signs. Checking identity, taking the history and examining stay with the cardiologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: History was copied from letters and the note typed after the visit.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured exchange of medication and diagnoses, and scribes that write back to the record.
tasks.still_hard: Referrals from abroad or on paper.
tasks.human_edge: Asking the follow-up question that reveals the real complaint.
tasks.altitude: Less copying and typing; the conversation stays.

reach.learn: Whether structured referrals reduce questions back.

evidence.claim: A scribe records the consultation, the clinician validates, and the note goes into the patient record.
Across 236,153 scribe notes, self-estimated time per note fell 29%; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: obtaining and recording patient information at intake; diagnosing (task 22700) and designing treatment plans (task 22698) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s3: medication and diagnoses arrive by structured exchange for about 60% of referrals; s3 is priced at that share.
s3 saves retyping medication lists and diagnoses from letters.
Patients' questionnaire time is shown in s1 and replaces part of the paper form they filled before.
A DPIA is done and the works council consents before the scribe is used.
unknowns: Share of referrals with structured data.

incremental.description: Cardiologist joins the monthly sample audit of notes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: paper referrals and little recording; high: structured referrals and most patients recorded.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide which tests are needed, explain them, enter orders for medical tests such as echocardiograms, electrocardiograms and angiograms, fill and sign external referrals, send them, and track pending tests.

steps.what: Cardiologist decides which medical tests the patient needs
Cardiologist explains the test to the patient
Cardiologist enters the test order with the clinical question, retyping the indication
Cardiologist fills the referral form for an external test centre
Cardiologist checks and signs the final referral
Cardiologist sends the referral to the test centre by fax or mail
Cardiologist keeps a list of pending tests and checks each one is scheduled and resulted

approvals.approved_version: The referral for the named patient and test, exactly as checked and signed by the cardiologist in s5, sent to the test centre named on it; any change needs a new signature.

tasks.design: Order sets per indication fill the clinical question and the required data from the note, instead of retyping the indication. External referrals are filled from the record. After the cardiologist signs, the referral goes through secure electronic exchange instead of fax or mail. A worklist shows ordered tests that are not yet scheduled or resulted, replacing the cardiologist's own list. Choosing tests and explaining them stay with the cardiologist; order sets only prefill and never choose a test.
tasks.previous_blocker: Indications were retyped and pending tests tracked on a personal list.
tasks.enabler_now: Order sets, electronic referrals and open-order worklists.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the one test that answers the question without extra risk.
tasks.altitude: Less form filling; test choice stays.

evidence.claim: Letters by e-mail or fax give way to structured exchange.
Decision software is usually a medical device of class IIa or higher; order sets that only prefill are not.

assumptions: Boundary: ordering tests; explaining procedures and results (task 22701) and diagnosing (task 22700) are sibling tasks.
s2 is part of explaining procedures, which sibling task 22701 covers; its saving is counted there.
Input contract for s4 and s6: about 60% of external test centres accept electronic referrals; s4 and s6 are priced at that share.
s3 saves retyping the indication already in the note; s7 replaces checking each patient by hand.
Deciding and explaining keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of tests sent to external centres.
research_questions: Are fewer ordered tests lost to follow-up?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly paper referrals; high: mostly in-house and electronic referrals.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
